texts: About 5 to 10 percent of patients with a parapneumonic effusion go on to develop an empyema: A is the answer.
The exudative stage responds to antibiotics and drainage; the fibrinopurulent stage usually needs more, such as tube drainage, fibrinolytics or VATS.
A low glucose and high LDH mark the fibrinopurulent stage, and pleural fluid cultures are positive in far fewer than 90 percent of patients.
